crates.name: molla-kernels
crates.purpose_one_line: WGSL compute-kernel catalog plus per-shader Rust dispatch wrappers (bind groups, uniform packing, upload/readback) — a GPU-primitive library, not a simulator.

loc_by_language.note: 68048 rs / 22866 wgsl / 61 toml = 90975. Rust splits 48167 src vs 19881 tests+benches. Tests are 29% of the Rust and 22% of all physical lines.

main_modules.actuator_* (7): actuator_delay, actuator_neural_lstm, actuator_neural_mlp, actuator_pd, actuator_pid, actuator_pipeline_pd, actuator_pipeline_pid — GPU halves of the controllers whose host halves live in molla-actuators
main_modules.rigid_body_dynamics: crba, rnea, featherstone, featherstone_adjoint, featherstone_adjoint_gpu, jacobian, integrate_bodies, dense3
main_modules.contact_and_broadphase: barrier_newton, contact_reduction, contact_sensor, hydroelastic, soft_bvh_gpu, soft_vt_contact, raycast, splat_raytrace
main_modules.optim: optim_adam, optim_sgd, robust_loss, dahl_friction, dahl_oracle, scan, fft

crates.top_public_types: 128 re-exported names in src/lib.rs:101-300. Largest clusters: TireFem* (~50 names), TireDem* (~35), TireVehicle* (~30), the geometry re-exports (EpaKernel/GjkKernel/MprKernel/LbvhBroadPhase) and the actuator kernels.

dependency_edges.cargo_claims: YES — crates/molla-kernels/Cargo.toml:37 `molla-vehicle = { path = "../molla-vehicle", optional = true }`, pulled in by the gpu feature at crates/molla-kernels/Cargo.toml:24 `"dep:molla-vehicle"`
dependency_edges.source_evidence: Only 4 real code tokens, all GPU-gated: crates/molla-kernels/src/tire_thermal.rs:505 and :539 (`snapshot: &molla_vehicle::TireRigSnapshot`), :579 (`snapshots: &[molla_vehicle::TireRigSnapshot]`), and crates/molla-kernels/src/tire_fem.rs:1404 (`tire: &molla_vehicle::TetraTireFem` in `tire_fem_gpu_input_from_tetra_fem`). 45 further hits are doc-comment cross-references only.
dependency_edges.direction_assessment: This is the single most important structural defect in the region. molla-kernels is the low-level GPU-primitive crate (dispatch wrappers over WGSL; 5138 `wgpu::` tokens vs 45 vehicle tokens). molla-vehicle is a high-level application/simulation crate that depends on NOTHING at all. So the arrow points low→high: the primitive library depends on the application. It is not a cycle — nothing in vehicle depends on kernels in Cargo — but the direction is backwards. All four uses are snapshot-adapter helpers (`*_from_rig_snapshot`, `*_from_tetra_fem`) that translate a vehicle-owned struct into a kernels-owned GPU input; they are vehicle-boundary code living in the kernel crate. Correct fix: delete the dep and move those four helpers into molla-vehicle (which already does `include_str!` on kernels' shaders anyway, observability.rs:124).

dependency_edges.cargo_claims: YES — crates/molla-actuators/Cargo.toml:27 `molla-kernels = { path = "../molla-kernels", default-features = false, optional = true }`, enabled via crates/molla-actuators/Cargo.toml:19 `"molla-kernels/gpu"`
dependency_edges.source_evidence: 10 real `molla_kernels::` tokens, e.g. crates/molla-actuators/src/controller_pd.rs:19 `use molla_kernels::ActuatorPdKernel;`, and the same pattern in controller_pid, controller_neural_mlp, controller_neural_lstm, controller_pipeline_pd, controller_pipeline_pid, delay, clamping/dc_motor, clamping/max_effort, clamping/position_based.
dependency_edges.direction_assessment: Points the right way: high-level host orchestration → low-level GPU dispatch. Each actuators controller owns a kernel and drives it (controller_pd.rs:38 `pub struct ControllerPd { kernel: ActuatorPdKernel, ... }`). No inversion.

dependency_edges.cargo_claims: NONE in molla-vehicle's Cargo.toml — the file is `[dependencies]` empty (crates/molla-vehicle/Cargo.toml:19-20)
dependency_edges.source_evidence: crates/molla-vehicle/src/real_tire/observability.rs:124-127 does `include_str!("../../../molla-kernels/shaders/tire_brush.wgsl")` and the three sibling shaders tire_fem/thermal/transient, to assert shader-contract strings.
dependency_edges.verdict: HIDDEN EDGE — vehicle→kernels at the filesystem level
dependency_edges.direction_assessment: This is the inverse of the Cargo edge above and nobody declared it. vehicle reaches into kernels' source tree; kernels reaches into vehicle's public API. Together they form a mutual entanglement that a Cargo-only reading misses entirely. It is unique in the workspace: no other crate include_str!'s across a crate boundary (every other include_str! is `../shaders/` within its own crate).

dependency_edges.source_evidence: Three facade forwarding surfaces: crates/molla/src/kernels/mod.rs:118 `pub use molla_kernels::...`, crates/molla/src/vehicle.rs:4 `pub use molla_vehicle::*;`, crates/molla/src/actuators/mod.rs:41,66 `pub use molla_actuators::{...}`.
dependency_edges.direction_assessment: The facade sits above all three and forwards them. It treats kernels and vehicle as independent siblings (both direct deps of `molla`), which is the intended shape — and the exact shape the kernels→vehicle edge violates.

dependency_edges.source_evidence: Genuine production use, not just re-export: crates/molla-solvers/src/semi_implicit.rs:38,45 (`molla_kernels::IntegrateBodiesKernel`), crates/molla-solvers/src/barrier_solver.rs:59,147,148,169,170.

dependency_edges.cargo_claims: crates/molla-vehicle/Cargo.toml:19-20 — `[dependencies]` is empty. Zero deps, not even molla-core or molla-math.
dependency_edges.source_evidence: Confirmed by `cargo metadata --no-deps` (see build_probe): molla-vehicle 'deps: []'. It defines its own scalar math helpers on raw `[f64; 3]` arrays instead: crates/molla-vehicle/src/real_tire/internal.rs:47 `pub(crate) fn dot`, :51 `pub(crate) fn cross`, plus duplicates in crates/molla-vehicle/src/tire.rs:290,299 and crates/molla-vehicle/src/granular.rs:453.
dependency_edges.direction_assessment: A 41k-loc physics crate that reimplements dot/cross locally and shares no type with molla-core/molla-math/molla-sim is disconnected from the engine it is named for. It is a self-contained island — which is why it could be depended on by kernels without a cycle, and also why its 'GPU parity' story is stitched together with include_str! and hand-rolled `[f64;3]` conversions rather than shared types.

dead_or_dormant.evidence: crates/molla-kernels/src/lib.rs:43,48 are the only un-gated `mod` lines; every other module is `#[cfg(feature = "gpu")]`. `dahl_oracle` is used only by crates/molla-solvers/tests/vbd_extended_gpu.rs:29,188,222 (a test) and the viewer at bin/molla_viewer/src/main.rs:10403 via the facade. dead_or_dormant.item: molla-kernels' production use is mostly facade re-export, not dispatch
dead_or_dormant.evidence: Of the ~56 `molla_kernels::` tokens outside the crate, 24 are one-line `pub use molla_kernels` forwards in crates/molla/src/kernels/*.rs and crates/molla/src/math/sparse_gpu.rs. Only molla-solvers (2 files), molla-sensors (5 files), molla-fem (3 files) and molla-actuators (10 files) actually dispatch a kernel. `grep -rn "molla_kernels::" bin/` returns ZERO — the viewer never names kernels directly; it goes through `molla::kernels`.
dead_or_dormant.risk: MEDIUM — a large share of kernels' 128 public types have no caller outside the facade forwarding them. Cannot prove per-type deadness without running `cargo check` (blocked; see build_probe), so this is a coverage limit, not a per-item verdict.

redundancy.what: kernels' actuator_* shader wrappers vs actuators' controller_* host layer
redundancy.evidence: kernels/src/actuator_pd.rs (201 loc, exports ActuatorPdKernel) vs actuators/src/controller_pd.rs (141 loc, `use molla_kernels::ActuatorPdKernel`). This is NOT duplication — it is a clean two-layer split. Worth stating because the near-identical names invite a mistaken merge.

redundancy.what: The molla facade's crates/molla/src/kernels/*.rs are almost all 3-line `pub use` shims
redundancy.evidence: 24 of the 29 files in crates/molla/src/kernels/ are ≤6 lines and forward verbatim (e.g. lbvh.rs is 3 lines, fft.rs 3 lines). The genuinely local ones forward to molla_fem, not molla_kernels: dg_swe_flux.rs, fem.rs, fem_*.rs (`pub use molla_fem::...`).
redundancy.note: Facade scaffolding, not logic duplication — but it inflates apparent module count.

redundancy.what: kernels' tire_* family (11 modules, 20+ shaders) overlaps molla-vehicle's real_tire/
redundancy.evidence: Every tire kernel has a CPU counterpart in vehicle: tire_brush.rs mirrors `molla_vehicle::real_tire::evaluate_brush_tire` (stated at kernels/src/tire_brush.rs:3), tire_fem.rs mirrors `molla_vehicle::TetraTireFem` (kernels/src/tire_fem.rs:3,1388,3199), tire_bekker.rs mirrors `DeformableTerrain` (tire_bekker.rs:3). CPU/GPU parity pairs are intentional, but the CPU side lives in vehicle and the GPU side in kernels — which is precisely why the inverted edge exists.
redundancy.note: This is the redundancy that CAUSES the inversion; fixing the layering addresses both.

connection_health.summary: The region has one real inversion and one undeclared hidden edge; everything else is layered correctly.
inverted_edges: molla-kernels → molla-vehicle (Cargo.toml:37) — primitive crate depends on application crate
undeclared_edges: molla-vehicle → molla-kernels via include_str! (observability.rs:124-127) — filesystem, not Cargo
missing_edges: molla-vehicle depends on nothing; it shares no type with molla-core/molla-math/molla-sim and reimplements dot/cross locally (internal.rs:47,51)
connection_health.cycle: NO true cycle in Cargo — nothing in vehicle declares kernels. But there IS a mutual entanglement once the include_str! edge is counted: kernels→vehicle (API) and vehicle→kernels (source files). Cargo cannot see it, so a Cargo-only layering check would pass while the code is still tangled.
proposed_layering: L0 (no molla deps): molla-core, molla-math, molla-storage
L2 (GPU primitives): molla-kernels — must depend ONLY on L0/L1. No molla-vehicle, ever.
L3 (domain host layers, parallel siblings): molla-actuators → kernels; molla-geometry → compute; molla-sim
L4 (domains dispatching kernels): molla-sensors, molla-fem, molla-solvers → kernels + actuators
L5 (application): molla-vehicle → core/math/sim (currently MISSING) + kernels (for GPU input types it already owns). It should own the snapshot-adapter functions.
L6 (facade): molla → all of L2-L5, keeping kernels and vehicle as independent siblings.

Concretely: (a) delete molla-kernels/Cargo.toml:37 and its gpu-feature entry at :24; (b) move tire_thermal_input_from_rig_snapshot / tire_thermal_state_from_rig_snapshot / tire_thermal_build_rig_replay_batch (tire_thermal.rs:504,538,578) and tire_fem_gpu_input_from_tetra_fem (tire_fem.rs:1403) into molla-vehicle::real_tire, which then depends on molla-kernels — the direction actually intended; (c) give molla-vehicle a real molla-core/molla-math dep so it stops reimplementing dot/cross; (d) replace the four include_str! reaches (observability.rs:124-127) with a declared shared shader-contract mechanism or move the assertion into kernels' own tests.
connection_health.vehicle_consumers: Besides the viewer (bin/molla_viewer, 300+ call sites) and the `molla` facade re-export (crates/molla/src/vehicle.rs:4), NOTHING depends on vehicles. crates/molla-vehicle is a dependency of exactly three artifacts: molla, molla_viewer, and (wrongly) molla-kernels. molla-solvers, molla-sim, molla-fem, molla-sensors do not use it.
connection_health.actuators_genericity: molla-actuators is GENUINELY GENERIC. grep for vehicle|terrain|tire across crates/molla-actuators/src returns 2 hits, both the word 'entirely' in a doc comment (controller_neural_lstm.rs:26, controller_neural_mlp.rs:4). Zero tire/terrain/vehicle coupling. It is correctly generic and reusable.

build_probe.conclusion: No compilation was achieved. Exit 101 is a RESOLUTION failure, not a compile error: cargo must resolve the whole workspace before it can build any single package, and the workspace contains bin/molla_viewer, which depends on the git dependency bevy_frost (branch develop, rev 001fc84aedcad2d9eebf4f4c1b093d7aa8acb9f1). That checkout cannot be created because CARGO_HOME (/pkg/cargo) has a read-only git/checkouts directory (/pkg/cargo itself is writable, but /pkg/cargo/git and /pkg/cargo/git/checkouts are read-only). A retry with a writable mirror of CARGO_HOME reached the network but failed DNS ('Temporary failure in name resolution' for github.com), and offline mode cannot checkout a rev absent from the local git db. Therefore every statement in this report about which kernel types are dead is derived from source greps, NOT from a compiler call graph — that is the main coverage limit. cargo metadata --no-deps DID succeed (exit 0), and it is what confirms molla-vehicle's empty dependency list.

limits: No compile or type-check completed (exit 101 at resolution, bevy_frost git checkout blocked by a read-only cargo cache; DNS fails on retry). All deadness claims are grep-derived, so a type used only through a generic/trait indirection or reached via a re-export alias I did not grep could be misclassified.
